title: American Cancer Society Recommends Prostate Cancer Screening
excerpt: In a policy shift, the American Cancer Society now advises prostate-specific antigen screening every two years for men aged 50 to 69 at average risk.
body_html: The American Cancer Society has updated its guidelines, now urging prostate cancer tests for all men who fall into a specific age and risk category. According to the updated guidance, men between the ages of 50 and 69 who face an average risk of the disease should undergo prostate-specific antigen screening every two years.
